title: Assistant identity and help
heading: Who are you?
text:
I am the Asset Pricing and Hedging Assistant, an AI learning guide to this finance
project. I am designed to explain its assumptions, methods, recorded results and
limitations in simple language. I am not the project author, the professor, a bank
representative or a personal financial adviser.
citation: Assistant identity and help — Who are you? [common]

title: Assistant identity and help
heading: What can you help me with?
text:
The prepared material covers the project story; shares and cash flows; CAPM and
WACC; DCF and NPV; currency hedges; option pricing and Greeks; portfolio allocation;
and the Ridge/gradient-boosting experiment. It also covers how to navigate the
website, where figures came from and what the analysis cannot prove. Ask a small
question such as “What is a share?” or “Why is future cash discounted?”

The offline helper includes simple greeting and help answers plus local keyword
retrieval. The website's chat integration can optionally send retrieved passages
to Gemini when the owner has configured a key and the visitor enables AI replies.
That connection must be reported from actual runtime settings, not assumed from
the presence of this document. Semantic retrieval and chatbot calculator access
are not implemented.
citation: Assistant identity and help — What can you help me with? [common]

title: Assistant identity and help
heading: How should I start if I do not know finance?
text:
Start with the business story: a hypothetical company spends money today to expand
and hopes to collect cash later. Learn what cash flow means, then present value
and NPV, then the required return, then currency protection. The portfolio/ML
comparison is a separate experiment and can be learned last. You can ask for
one step, a smaller example, or an explanation without equations.
citation: Assistant identity and help — How should I start if I do not know finance? [common]

title: Assistant identity and help
heading: Are you Gemini or ChatGPT? Were you trained on this project?
text:
Gemini is the supported answer provider for the optional website integration.
Whether it is configured and enabled depends on the running app; the offline
knowledge-base helper makes no model calls. The assistant is an application
interface, not a new foundation model trained by the project author. Local
retrieval selects relevant project passages for a pretrained model to explain.
This does not fine-tune that model or turn the portfolio forecast into a chatbot.
citation: Assistant identity and help — Are you Gemini or ChatGPT? Were you trained on this project? [common]

title: Assistant identity and help
heading: Can you fetch current prices, run calculations or trade?
text:
No live-market feed or trading connection is part of this assistant. The saved
figures are historical and the website's calculators are hypothetical. Chatbot
calculator access is a separate planned feature, not active just because a
calculator exists elsewhere on the site. The assistant must not claim to have
executed a new calculation without a trusted result from that calculator.
citation: Assistant identity and help — Can you fetch current prices, run calculations or trade? [common]

title: Assistant identity and help
heading: Can you help me prepare for an interview?
text:
The material can help explain what a method does, why the project used it, what
the original experiment produced and which assumptions limit the result. It must
not invent personal contributions, backdate later work, hide genuine shortcomings
or guarantee an interview outcome. Ask “Explain the original portfolio method”
or “What limitations should I mention about the hedge comparison?”
citation: Assistant identity and help — Can you help me prepare for an interview? [common]

title: Assistant identity and help
heading: Do you remember me or need my API key?
text:
Permanent personal memory is not implemented. The website interface can provide
a few recent session messages as context; this is not permanent memory. Clear
chat removes the visible transcript and the context used for future questions.
Users should never paste API keys into the conversation. The app owner configures
any provider key privately on the server; visitors do not need to see it.
citation: Assistant identity and help — Do you remember me or need my API key? [common]

title: Project overview and website navigation
heading: What is this project about?
text:
Asset Pricing and Hedging is an educational finance project with three related
but separate questions. First, is an illustrative business expansion worth its
upfront cost? Second, how can a company protect dollar receipts from exchange-rate
changes? Third, do return forecasts from simple ML models improve a portfolio
allocation experiment? Python implements the calculations and Streamlit presents
the analysis interactively.
citation: Project overview and website navigation — What is this project about? [common]

title: Project overview and website navigation
heading: How are the three parts connected—and not connected?
text:
The expansion uses assumed future business cash and a required return. Currency
hedging changes the rupees received for dollars. The portfolio experiment compares
investment-allocation rules on a separate five-asset universe. The portfolio is
not the expansion's financing plan. Its weights do not determine WACC, and ML
does not set the company's hedge. A forward-path project NPV is not automatically
the NPV of the separately discussed collar strategy.
citation: Project overview and website navigation — How are the three parts connected—and not connected? [common]

title: Project overview and website navigation
heading: Is this an actual Infosys expansion or investment recommendation?
text:
No evidence in this project establishes an announced Infosys expansion or a real
investment mandate. Infosys is the public reference company for the Indian equity
risk/valuation exercise. Project cash flows are illustrative assumptions, not
management guidance, realised profits or customer sales forecasts. A positive
case NPV means the labelled assumptions clear the chosen hurdle, not that an
investor should buy Infosys or that management should actually spend the money.
citation: Project overview and website navigation — Is this an actual Infosys expansion or investment recommendation? [common]

title: Project overview and website navigation
heading: Who created it and what is the course connection?
text:
The repository is maintained under the public account `arathii23`, and the project
is presented by Aaditya Rathi. The user-provided résumé credits Prof. Wasim Ahmed,
IIT Kanpur, ECO423 and gives a May–July 2025 period. These are attribution/context
records, not independent evidence of supervision, a grade, endorsement, or which
person wrote each component. The visible saved market snapshot is from 2026;
do not claim those figures existed in 2025 or invent the author's personal role.
citation: Project overview and website navigation — Who created it and what is the course connection? [common]

title: Project overview and website navigation
heading: How do I use the website?
text:
Start at Overview for the case and the main findings. Expansion & valuation
contains project cash flows, scenario inputs, cost of capital and Gordon share
valuation. Currency hedging compares protection of dollar receipts. Portfolio
analysis compares allocation rules and their risks. Option pricing lets visitors
change model inputs. Methods & data contains definitions, assumptions and
downloads. Changing a scenario is not the same as changing the recorded base case.
citation: Project overview and website navigation — How do I use the website? [common]

title: Project overview and website navigation
heading: What technology and data does it use?
text:
The finance implementation uses Python, NumPy, pandas and scikit-learn, with
Streamlit for the interface and plotting tools for charts. Public Yahoo Finance
series are the recorded price inputs. The Indian government-bond rate failed to
load in the original pull, so a labelled fallback was used. The exact tickers,
sample dates, numerical results and implementation details must be taken from
the selected version rather than inferred from a general project description.
citation: Project overview and website navigation — What technology and data does it use? [common]

title: Project overview and website navigation
heading: What are the public project links?
text:
Repository: https://github.com/arathii23/asset-pricing-and-hedging

Website: https://asset-pricing-and-hedging-desk.streamlit.app/

These identify the project, not a promise that a particular local extension is
already deployed. A chatbot should not claim it has opened or checked either link
unless the application has actually supplied a current verification result.
citation: Project overview and website navigation — What are the public project links? [common]

title: Shares, investors, borrowing and business cash flows
heading: What is a share and who is a shareholder?
text:
A share is a small unit of ownership in a company. Someone owning shares is a
shareholder. Owning a share is not the same as owning a fixed amount of cash in
the company's bank account. A shareholder may receive dividends and may gain or
lose money as the market price changes.

When someone buys an existing listed share, the payment normally goes to its
previous owner, not to the company. A new share issue can raise fresh money for
the company. Do not describe every stock-market purchase as directly financing
the illustrative expansion.
citation: Shares, investors, borrowing and business cash flows — What is a share and who is a shareholder? [common]

title: Shares, investors, borrowing and business cash flows
heading: How can shareholders earn money? Must a good expansion raise the share price?
text:
Shareholders can receive dividends, if declared, and can sell shares for more than
they paid, if the price rises. Neither is guaranteed. Prices respond to expected
future cash, risk, interest rates and information already reflected in the market.
An expansion reporting positive cash flow does not mechanically guarantee a
higher share price: investors may have expected even better results.
citation: Shares, investors, borrowing and business cash flows — How can shareholders earn money? Must a good expansion raise the share price? [common]

title: Shares, investors, borrowing and business cash flows
heading: How are shareholders different from lenders?
text:
Shareholders provide ownership capital and bear the residual business risk.
Lenders provide borrowed money under a contract and expect repayment and interest.
Lenders generally have priority over shareholders, but loans can still default.
Interest is often less risky than equity returns, not universally “small” or
guaranteed. A loan is not the same as buying shares in the company.
citation: Shares, investors, borrowing and business cash flows — How are shareholders different from lenders? [common]

title: Shares, investors, borrowing and business cash flows
heading: Why borrow if the company already has money?
text:
A company may preserve an operating cash buffer, spread financing across sources,
or match borrowing to a specific investment. Having some cash does not mean every
rupee is available for a new project. Borrowing also creates interest and repayment
obligations; it is not automatically beneficial. This case does not establish that
Infosys took a particular loan for the illustrative expansion.
citation: Shares, investors, borrowing and business cash flows — Why borrow if the company already has money? [common]

title: Shares, investors, borrowing and business cash flows
heading: Is almost 100% equity funding the same as all cash being shareholders' money?
text:
No. A market-value equity weight used in WACC is a financing-value ratio, not a
breakdown of the bank balance. Company cash can reflect customer collections,
retained earnings, borrowing, new equity and other transactions. A business can
have little recorded debt without all current cash having been freshly deposited
by shareholders. Market capitalisation is not the company's available cash.
citation: Shares, investors, borrowing and business cash flows — Is almost 100% equity funding the same as all cash being shareholders' money? [common]

title: Shares, investors, borrowing and business cash flows
heading: What is an expansion and who generates the later cash flows?
text:
An expansion means spending now to add business capacity or operations, such as
new facilities, delivery capability or services. In this hypothetical case, the
expanded business generates later cash through its operations. Customers pay the
business; costs and investment needs use some of that cash; the remaining assumed
free cash is used in the valuation. Shareholders are not assumed to deposit the
year-one, year-two and year-three cash flows themselves.
citation: Shares, investors, borrowing and business cash flows — What is an expansion and who generates the later cash flows? [common]

title: Shares, investors, borrowing and business cash flows
heading: Are free cash flow, revenue, profit and dividends the same?
text:
No. Revenue records sales. Accounting profit follows accounting recognition and
expense rules. Free cash flow is cash remaining after the operating costs, cash
taxes and investment needs included in the model. A dividend is cash the company
chooses to distribute to shareholders. This expansion uses unlevered project cash
before financing payments; it does not assume every rupee is paid as a dividend.

The original version specifies the net cash-flow assumptions directly. A later
review adds an illustrative collections/cost/reinvestment breakdown. Do not claim
that breakdown was observed company data or existed in the original version.
citation: Shares, investors, borrowing and business cash flows — Are free cash flow, revenue, profit and dividends the same? [common]

title: Discounting, DCF and NPV
heading: Why is future money discounted?
text:
Money available now can be used now, while a future receipt involves waiting and
risk. Discounting translates a future payment into an equivalent value today
under a chosen required return. In a toy example, at 10% per year, ₹110 arriving
in one year has a present value of ₹110 / 1.10 = ₹100. A year-two receipt is divided
by 1.10 twice. This toy 10% rate is not the project's recorded WACC.
citation: Discounting, DCF and NPV — Why is future money discounted? [common]

title: Discounting, DCF and NPV
heading: What is DCF and how does NPV differ?
text:
Discounted cash flow (DCF) is the method of valuing assumed future cash today.
Net present value (NPV) adds the discounted future inflows and subtracts the
investment paid today. With an outflow at time zero, NPV = cash_0 + cash_1/(1+r)
+ cash_2/(1+r)^2 + cash_3/(1+r)^3. A positive result clears the chosen hurdle under
the assumptions; it is not a realised profit, a bank balance or a guaranteed return.
citation: Discounting, DCF and NPV — What is DCF and how does NPV differ? [common]

title: Discounting, DCF and NPV
heading: Why does the WACC percentage appear in the cash-flow calculation?
text:
There are two different questions: how much cash might arrive, and what return is
required to justify waiting and taking risk? The cash-flow assumptions answer the
first; WACC supplies the required-return proxy for the second. WACC is the `r` in
the discounting formula. It is not an extra annual cash receipt and is not added
to the cash flows. In this teaching case, the company rate is used as a proxy for
a project assumed to have similar risk; a real expansion may need a different rate.
citation: Discounting, DCF and NPV — Why does the WACC percentage appear in the cash-flow calculation? [common]

title: Discounting, DCF and NPV
heading: What does IRR mean? Is it the same as WACC?
text:
The internal rate of return (IRR) is the discount rate that would make a cash-flow
stream's NPV zero. For this case's single initial outflow followed by positive
inflows, it can be compared with WACC. IRR is calculated from the assumed cash;
WACC is the externally chosen hurdle proxy. An IRR above WACC is consistent with
positive NPV here. IRR is not a promised stock return, and unusual cash-flow sign
patterns can make IRR ambiguous or unsuitable.
citation: Discounting, DCF and NPV — What does IRR mean? Is it the same as WACC? [common]

title: Discounting, DCF and NPV
heading: What is sensitivity analysis and a break-even cash-flow haircut?
text:
Sensitivity analysis changes an assumption and observes how the result changes.
A cash-flow haircut reduces each future payment by the same fraction. The
break-even haircut is the reduction that brings NPV to zero. It is a cushion under
the stated assumptions, not a probability of loss. FX shocks on future receipts
should not change a cost already paid today; an original batch tornado changed
both, which is a documented limitation distinct from the later future-only test.
citation: Discounting, DCF and NPV — What is sensitivity analysis and a break-even cash-flow haircut? [common]

title: Discounting, DCF and NPV
heading: How do crore, million and billion relate?
text:
₹1 crore = ₹10 million. ₹1 billion = ₹100 crore. ₹1 million = ₹0.1 crore.
USD million and INR million are different currencies: multiply a dollar amount
by rupees per dollar before expressing it in rupees. A rate per USD, a per-share
price and a total project value must not be mixed.

For the original project's full rupee calculation, use its versioned cash-flow
table. Its approximately ₹8.37 **billion** present value is approximately ₹837
crore, not ₹8.37 million. The original NPV is the smaller amount after subtracting
the upfront investment—not the entire present value of future inflows.
citation: Discounting, DCF and NPV — How do crore, million and billion relate? [common]

title: Discounting, DCF and NPV
heading: Is there a terminal value or salvage payment after year three?
text:
The recorded teaching expansion ends after three years with zero salvage. It does
not include a continuing business terminal value. Gordon equity valuation, which
assumes dividends continuing forever, is a separate calculation. Never add that
share value to this project's final cash flow or describe the expansion as a full
company enterprise-value DCF.
citation: Discounting, DCF and NPV — Is there a terminal value or salvage payment after year three? [common]

title: Expected return, CAPM, WACC and Gordon valuation
heading: What does expected return mean and where does it come from?
text:
“Return” can mean different things. A historical return is measured from past
prices. A forecast is an estimate of a later return. A required return is the
compensation investors demand for waiting and taking risk. In the project's CAPM
calculation, the model-implied required equity return is used as a hurdle input;
it is not a guarantee that shareholders or the expansion will earn that amount.
The portfolio's historical/ML expected-return estimates are different inputs.
citation: Expected return, CAPM, WACC and Gordon valuation — What does expected return mean and where does it come from? [common]

title: Expected return, CAPM, WACC and Gordon valuation
heading: What are market risk and beta? Why use the stock here?
text:
Market risk comes from broad events that can affect many investments together,
such as economy-wide shocks. Beta estimates how a stock's returns co-move with a
market benchmark. It does not measure every business risk or guarantee an exact
move next week. Infosys stock versus Nifty provides a reference estimate for the
return equity investors require; it does not mean investors buy stock to provide
each future project cash flow. The expansion rate relies on a similar-risk proxy
assumption, not an independently estimated project beta.
citation: Expected return, CAPM, WACC and Gordon valuation — What are market risk and beta? Why use the stock here? [common]

title: Expected return, CAPM, WACC and Gordon valuation
heading: How does CAPM combine the risk-free rate and equity risk premium?
text:
CAPM required equity return = risk-free rate + beta × equity risk premium.
The risk-free rate is a starting government-bond proxy; the premium is assumed
extra compensation for stock-market risk. They are not two versions of the same
rate. The original project uses a labelled 6.50% India fallback and a 5.50% assumed
equity risk premium. Its estimated beta is about 0.81, producing about 10.96%.
The exact figures are in the original-version facts. The fallback is not today's
live government-bond yield and the premium is not estimated by subtracting 5.50
from 6.50. A short-sample market premium is reported separately.
citation: Expected return, CAPM, WACC and Gordon valuation — How does CAPM combine the risk-free rate and equity risk premium? [common]

title: Expected return, CAPM, WACC and Gordon valuation
heading: What is WACC and why is it close to the equity return?
text:
Weighted average cost of capital combines the equity required return with the
after-tax borrowing cost: WACC = equity_weight × cost_of_equity + debt_weight ×
cost_of_debt × (1 − tax). The original saved market-value equity weight is almost
100%, so debt has very little influence. WACC is approximately, not exactly, the
cost of equity. The weights do not say what the company has in its bank account.
The project uses a frozen capital-mix input, not a new expansion loan or a target
financing plan reconstructed from company filings.
citation: Expected return, CAPM, WACC and Gordon valuation — What is WACC and why is it close to the equity return? [common]

title: Expected return, CAPM, WACC and Gordon valuation
heading: Why use bond yield instead of coupon as the cost of debt?
text:
A coupon is the contracted interest payment relative to face value. Yield to
maturity depends on the price paid and the bond's future payments; it is a better
illustration of the borrowing return required at that price. The project's bond
is a labelled comparable-method example, not a verified Infosys expansion bond.
Duration approximates small price sensitivity to yield changes; convexity adds
curvature. The tax rate is a modelling assumption, not personalised tax advice.
citation: Expected return, CAPM, WACC and Gordon valuation — Why use bond yield instead of coupon as the cost of debt? [common]

title: Expected return, CAPM, WACC and Gordon valuation
heading: What does the market-plus-FX factor model add?
text:
The cross-check regresses Infosys excess returns on market excess returns and
USDINR returns. The market premium is overridden with the labelled assumption;
the FX contribution uses a historical premium. It is an alternative required-
return estimate, not a causal explanation of every stock move or a proven rule
that adding FX always improves WACC. The base expansion uses CAPM-based WACC.
Mastercard versus the S&P 500 is a separate US comparison, not an Indian holding.
citation: Expected return, CAPM, WACC and Gordon valuation — What does the market-plus-FX factor model add? [common]

title: Expected return, CAPM, WACC and Gordon valuation
heading: What does Gordon dividend valuation estimate?
text:
The Gordon model values a share from assumed dividends growing forever:
share_value = next_dividend / (required_equity_return − perpetual_growth).
Growth must be below the required return. The original illustration grows its
saved trailing dividend by an assumed 5%; this is not verified future guidance.
The resulting value is not a cash dividend or the value of the expansion. A
market price above the model can reflect different growth, payout or risk
expectations; it does not prove the stock is overpriced.
citation: Expected return, CAPM, WACC and Gordon valuation — What does Gordon dividend valuation estimate? [common]

title: Expected return, CAPM, WACC and Gordon valuation
heading: What does the reported implied growth mean?
text:
The implementation holds the already-computed next dividend fixed, then calculates
required_return − next_dividend/market_price. That is the reported implied-growth
cross-check. It does not jointly re-estimate next dividend as growth changes, so
do not confuse it with solving price = trailing_dividend × (1+g)/(required_return−g)
for g. The exact recorded estimate belongs to the selected version and assumptions.
citation: Expected return, CAPM, WACC and Gordon valuation — What does the reported implied growth mean? [common]

title: Dollar receipts, currency risk and hedge choices
heading: What is USDINR and why does a dollar recipient face currency risk?
text:
USDINR means rupees for one US dollar. At 90 INR/USD, receiving USD 1m gives
₹90m. At 85 it gives ₹85m. These are toy rates, not the project snapshot.
When USDINR falls, the rupee strengthens and a fixed dollar receipt buys fewer
rupees. When it rises, the dollar strengthens and the recipient benefits.
The operating business can perform as planned while currency conversion still
changes its rupee cash receipts.
citation: Dollar receipts, currency risk and hedge choices — What is USDINR and why does a dollar recipient face currency risk? [common]

title: Dollar receipts, currency risk and hedge choices
heading: What does a currency hedge do? What does it not do?
text:
A hedge changes how an identified exposure responds to exchange rates. It can
reduce uncertainty, but may cost money or give up upside. It does not create
customer sales, remove operating risk or guarantee that the expansion succeeds.
Hedge only the confirmed exposure: if receipts fail to arrive, a forward or a
sold call can leave obligations without the expected dollars to cover them.
citation: Dollar receipts, currency risk and hedge choices — What does a currency hedge do? What does it not do? [common]

title: Dollar receipts, currency risk and hedge choices
heading: How does a forward work and where does its rate come from?
text:
A forward agrees today on the rate for exchanging currencies on a future date.
For a fully covered fixed dollar receipt, the rupee amount is notional × forward
rate, before real-world costs and credit effects. Certainty means giving up both
unfavourable and favourable future spot movements.

The project's covered-interest-parity illustration uses spot, INR and USD rates,
tenor, a two-business-day spot lag and ACT/365 INR versus ACT/360 USD conventions.
The simple intuition is F ≈ S × (1 + INR interest)/(1 + USD interest).
The implementation uses the actual tenor/day-count conventions rather than that
rough one-year shorthand. A forward rate is a no-arbitrage pricing relationship,
not a forecast of where spot will actually end up. The versioned result record
contains its saved value.
citation: Dollar receipts, currency risk and hedge choices — How does a forward work and where does its rate come from? [common]

title: Dollar receipts, currency risk and hedge choices
heading: How does a put protect a dollar receipt?
text:
A USD put gives the buyer the right to sell dollars at an agreed strike K.
Combined with a final-fixing dollar receipt, the gross effective rate is
max(final USDINR, K). The buyer pays a premium, so the net floor is lower.
The recipient keeps favourable dollar appreciation. A premium quoted INR/USD
must be multiplied by the USD notional to obtain a total rupee cost.
citation: Dollar receipts, currency risk and hedge choices — How does a put protect a dollar receipt? [common]

title: Dollar receipts, currency risk and hedge choices
heading: What is a collar and why is it not free protection?
text:
For this dollar recipient, buy a USD put at a lower strike and sell a USD call at
a higher strike. The call premium helps pay for the put. Gross proceeds per USD
are bounded between the two strikes: min(max(final rate, put strike), call strike).
Subtract the net premium on a consistent settlement-date basis for net proceeds.

The floor protects against a weaker dollar, but the sold call caps the benefit
of a stronger dollar. Even a zero-upfront-premium collar gives up upside and
creates a sold-option obligation. The recorded collar has a small positive model
premium, not exactly zero. It is not universally better than a forward or put.
citation: Dollar receipts, currency risk and hedge choices — What is a collar and why is it not free protection? [common]

title: Dollar receipts, currency risk and hedge choices
heading: What does 25-delta mean? Is it a 25% hedge?
text:
Delta is an option-price sensitivity. A 25-delta put has delta near −0.25 under
the chosen pricing convention; a 25-delta call has delta near +0.25. The code
solves for strikes with those model sensitivities. It does not mean that only
25% of the dollar notional is hedged, or that an option has a guaranteed 25%
probability of exercise. Hedge ratio is a separate choice about notional coverage.
citation: Dollar receipts, currency risk and hedge choices — What does 25-delta mean? Is it a 25% hedge? [common]

title: Dollar receipts, currency risk and hedge choices
heading: Why must average-rate protection match the receipt contract?
text:
A final-fixing receipt converts at one end-date rate. An average-indexed receipt
converts using the arithmetic average of agreed fixings. These are different
exposures even if the final rate is identical. An average-rate put pays
max(K − average rate, 0); a terminal put pays max(K − final rate, 0).
Matching notional alone does not fix this basis risk.

The original version priced an Asian CALL as an option illustration, not a
matched average-rate downside hedge for dollar receipts. Only the later local
review adds a matched average-rate PUT comparison. In that later example all
receipts settle at year-end; it does not model twelve actual monthly collections.
Use the version-specific evidence before describing what was implemented.
citation: Dollar receipts, currency risk and hedge choices — Why must average-rate protection match the receipt contract? [common]

title: Dollar receipts, currency risk and hedge choices
heading: Is the displayed hedge dispersion a forecast of risk?
text:
No. The original table takes 61 equally spaced exchange-rate outcomes from
15% below to 15% above the saved spot and calculates the standard deviation of
their proceeds. Those outcomes are scenarios, not probability-weighted forecasts.
Its dispersion reduction is not a VaR estimate, an observed realised saving or
an assertion that currency risk has fallen by that amount in the real world.
It excludes dealer spreads, counterparty default, collateral, basis and hedge
accounting. Model volatility is historical, not a dealer-implied FX quote.
citation: Dollar receipts, currency risk and hedge choices — Is the displayed hedge dispersion a forecast of risk? [common]

title: Dollar receipts, currency risk and hedge choices
heading: Does hedging automatically increase NPV or reduce WACC?
text:
No. In this project the flat-spot and forward-path DCF use the same WACC.
Only the assumed future FX conversion path changes; today’s investment remains
at today's spot. A higher forward-path NPV here is scenario arithmetic, not free
value creation or a proof that the business risk disappeared. A rigorous
cross-currency valuation needs consistent cash-flow, discount-rate and risk
assumptions; this is a labelled teaching approximation.
citation: Dollar receipts, currency risk and hedge choices — Does hedging automatically increase NPV or reduce WACC? [common]

title: Options, binomial, Black-Scholes, Greeks and average-rate pricing
heading: What are a call, put, strike, premium and expiry?
text:
A call gives its buyer the right to buy an underlying at an agreed strike. A put
gives the right to sell. The premium is paid for that right, and expiry limits
when the contract can be exercised. The seller takes the matching obligation.
Buying a put is therefore not the same as shorting a call: their obligations and
upside differ. Exercise style, currency, notional and settlement terms matter.
citation: Options, binomial, Black-Scholes, Greeks and average-rate pricing — What are a call, put, strike, premium and expiry? [common]

title: Options, binomial, Black-Scholes, Greeks and average-rate pricing
heading: What does the binomial or CRR model calculate?
text:
The Cox–Ross–Rubinstein tree lets the underlying move up or down in each small
time step. Start with each final option payoff, then work backwards by taking a
risk-neutral weighted payoff and discounting it. Risk-neutral probabilities are
pricing weights, not estimated real-world frequencies. A valid tree requires
probabilities between zero and one. More steps usually improve approximation
but finite-step prices can oscillate. The later review raises on invalid tree
probabilities; the original routine clipped them, which is a limitation.
citation: Options, binomial, Black-Scholes, Greeks and average-rate pricing — What does the binomial or CRR model calculate? [common]

title: Options, binomial, Black-Scholes, Greeks and average-rate pricing
heading: What is Black–Scholes and how does the FX version differ?
text:
Black–Scholes prices a European option under assumptions such as lognormal
underlying dynamics, constant volatility and rates, and idealised trading.
Dividend yield adjusts an equity implementation. For FX, the foreign interest
rate plays the corresponding yield role: INR is domestic and USD foreign when
the underlying is quoted INR per USD. This is the Garman–Kohlhagen adjustment.
The models are approximations, not a promise of a dealer's executable price.
citation: Options, binomial, Black-Scholes, Greeks and average-rate pricing — What is Black–Scholes and how does the FX version differ? [common]

title: Options, binomial, Black-Scholes, Greeks and average-rate pricing
heading: What are delta, gamma, vega and theta?
text:
Delta estimates the price change for a small underlying-price increase. Gamma
describes how delta changes. Vega describes sensitivity to volatility; theta
describes sensitivity to the passage of time with other inputs held fixed.
They are local model sensitivities, not guaranteed profits or exact large-move
predictions. The archived ADR vega is per unit volatility (a 1.00 absolute change),
not per one percentage point: multiply it by 0.01 for that convention. Its theta
is per year, not per day. Delta hedge quantities also depend on contract size.
citation: Options, binomial, Black-Scholes, Greeks and average-rate pricing — What are delta, gamma, vega and theta? [common]

title: Options, binomial, Black-Scholes, Greeks and average-rate pricing
heading: Did matching the option mid independently validate Black–Scholes?
text:
No. In the original ADR example the code solved for implied volatility from the
same saved mid-price, then plugged that volatility back into Black–Scholes.
Matching that mid is calibration by construction. Comparing the CRR tree using
the same inputs checks numerical agreement between models; it is not independent
market validation. The saved contract is a USD-denominated INFY ADR call, separate
from the INR-listed share and from the FX hedging options.

The original raw bid/ask and simultaneous underlying spot are not frozen with
the record. A listed ADR option may also have exercise-style features that a
European model does not capture. Do not claim dealer accuracy or a fully
reconstructable market quote from this archive.
citation: Options, binomial, Black-Scholes, Greeks and average-rate pricing — Did matching the option mid independently validate Black–Scholes? [common]

title: Options, binomial, Black-Scholes, Greeks and average-rate pricing
heading: What is an Asian arithmetic-average option and Monte Carlo pricing?
text:
An Asian payoff uses an average over specified observation dates. The code
simulates 40,000 risk-neutral exchange-rate paths with 12 future monthly fixings
and seed 7, computes each payoff, averages the payoffs and discounts to today.
Fixing dates exclude an initial spot fixing in this setup. A fixed seed supports
reproducibility, not accuracy certification. Sampling error and model assumptions
remain. These are pricing paths, not actual forecasts of the exchange rate.

The original illustration compared an at-the-money Asian CALL with a vanilla
CALL; their different payoffs mean a lower price is not proof of an equally
effective cheaper hedge. A dollar recipient needs downside protection, for which
the later matched example uses a PUT. Do not describe that later feature as part
of the original calculation.
citation: Options, binomial, Black-Scholes, Greeks and average-rate pricing — What is an Asian arithmetic-average option and Monte Carlo pricing? [common]

title: Options, binomial, Black-Scholes, Greeks and average-rate pricing
heading: What does a useful numerical check establish?
text:
Tree convergence, put-call parity and finite-difference checks of formula Greeks
can catch implementation errors under the same assumptions. The later review
contains such formula/numerical comparisons. Passing checks does not validate
future prices, market liquidity, exercise-style suitability or the truth of the
input assumptions. Keep calibration, numerical verification and real-world
validation separate.
citation: Options, binomial, Black-Scholes, Greeks and average-rate pricing — What does a useful numerical check establish? [common]

title: Portfolio allocation and ML
heading: What is a portfolio weight and what is this portfolio investing in?
text:
A portfolio is a collection of investments. A 20% weight puts one fifth of its
value into an asset; weights sum to 100% for a fully invested book. The experiment
uses Infosys, HDFC Bank, Reliance, Hindustan Unilever and GoldBeES. GoldBeES is a
gold ETF, not a fifth operating company. These are historical allocation tests,
not an actual company investment account or a live trading service.
Mastercard is a separate global comparator and is not held in this five-asset book.
citation: Portfolio allocation and ML — What is a portfolio weight and what is this portfolio investing in? [common]

title: Portfolio allocation and ML
heading: What does mean-variance allocation use?
text:
It uses estimated returns (means), how much each asset varies (variance), and how
assets move together (covariance). Diversification is about their combined risk,
not merely owning many names. Ledoit–Wolf shrinkage stabilises a noisy covariance
estimate; it cannot make expected returns reliable or guarantee diversification
in a crisis. The particular allocation algorithm differs by project version.
The original uses a clipped tangency-weight heuristic; the later review searches
a constrained 5-percentage-point weight grid. Do not call either a proof of the
globally optimal real-world portfolio.
citation: Portfolio allocation and ML — What does mean-variance allocation use? [common]

title: Portfolio allocation and ML
heading: What do Ridge and gradient boosting predict?
text:
They predict each asset's next-week return from earlier return patterns: own
return lags, Nifty returns, USDINR returns and rolling volatility. Ridge is linear
regression with a penalty that discourages large coefficients. Histogram gradient
boosting combines small decision trees for nonlinear patterns. Neither understands
company accounts or reads financial news here. The model does not set CAPM, WACC
or the FX hedge; the ML branch is a separate portfolio allocation experiment.
citation: Portfolio allocation and ML — What do Ridge and gradient boosting predict? [common]

title: Portfolio allocation and ML
heading: What does walk-forward mean and why not use a random split?
text:
Train on earlier observations, predict the next period, then move forward.
The setup starts after 104 eligible training weeks and refits every four weeks.
The features at information date t predict the return labelled t+1. Actual
trading would also need a feasible execution time after those inputs are known;
this weekly study does not prove a zero-delay executable strategy.

A random split can let later market conditions inform earlier predictions. In a
proper walk-forward pipeline even preprocessing learns only from training data.
The original Ridge did not scale its features; training-only StandardScaler was
added in the later review. Chronological forecasts do not eliminate retrospective
universe selection, strategy-selection bias or the need for an untouched holdout.
citation: Portfolio allocation and ML — What does walk-forward mean and why not use a random split? [common]

title: Portfolio allocation and ML
heading: How are forecasts turned into weights? Was Ridge allocated originally?
text:
The gradient-boosting allocation blends 20% model forecast with 80% expanding
historical mean before allocation. This is a cautious forecast tilt, not an
80% cash holding or 20% portfolio allocation to a model. Historical allocation
instead uses trailing 52-week means. Both covariance and rebalance rules matter.

The original tests Ridge forecast error but has no separate Ridge allocation
track. The later review adds one and also an expanding-mean allocation baseline
sharing the ML lookback. It is not accurate to say both models independently
produced the original portfolio score.
citation: Portfolio allocation and ML — How are forecasts turned into weights? Was Ridge allocated originally? [common]

title: Portfolio allocation and ML
heading: What do 0.30 Sharpe and 0.22 Nifty mean?
text:
Sharpe = (annualised average return − annual risk-free rate) / annualised return
volatility. The code annualises weekly arithmetic mean with 52 and standard
deviation with sqrt(52), using sample standard deviation. Sharpe is dimensionless:
0.30 is not 30% return, 30% accuracy or a forecast. It describes excess return per
unit of variability in the tested sample.

For the original résumé version, historical allocation rounds to 0.30 and the
Nifty price reference to 0.22. That is a modest sample comparison, not proof of a
durable edge. Exact values, method and dates belong to the version-specific
result document. Do not attach those original scores to the later algorithm.
citation: Portfolio allocation and ML — What do 0.30 Sharpe and 0.22 Nifty mean? [common]

title: Portfolio allocation and ML
heading: Why is the Nifty comparison limited?
text:
The price reference is Yahoo's ^NSEI, not Nifty TRI. Adjusted equity returns
include dividend adjustments, while a price index excludes dividends. Thus the
comparison is not a dividend-matched test of market outperformance. A future
matched study could use Nifty TRI or a dividend-adjusted investable ETF and
appropriate costs. This change has not been silently substituted in the record.

NSE explains that a total-return index includes both price movements and dividend
reinvestment: [NSE Indices — Total Return Index](https://www.niftyindices.com/resources/index-concepts/total-return-index).
citation: Portfolio allocation and ML — Why is the Nifty comparison limited? [common]

title: Portfolio allocation and ML
heading: What are transaction costs, turnover, drawdown and forecast error?
text:
Turnover measures how much holdings change; costs reduce returns when trading.
The study uses 10 basis points (0.10%) per unit of half-L1 one-way turnover.
Real costs also depend on spread, impact and instrument. Original active weights
stay fixed between rebalances, initial entry is not fully charged and equal
weight has free weekly rebalancing. Later code adds weight drift, initial entry
and a costed four-week equal-weight comparator. These differences affect results.

Maximum drawdown is the worst fall from an earlier portfolio-value peak. The
later review includes starting NAV in that check. RMSE measures average squared
prediction error on the return scale; sign hit rate counts correct directions.
Good RMSE need not give good net portfolio returns. Always compare with a simple
historical forecast and a matched allocation baseline, not just a complicated model.
citation: Portfolio allocation and ML — What are transaction costs, turnover, drawdown and forecast error? [common]

title: Portfolio allocation and ML
heading: What can I honestly say about the ML conclusion?
text:
The original historical allocation beats its GB challenger on sample Sharpe;
the original INFY GB forecast also has worse RMSE than its historical baseline.
This is useful negative evidence, not an ML success story that needs hiding.
The later Ridge allocation has only a small sample advantage over its matched
expanding-mean baseline. There is no untouched strategy-selection holdout or
statistical proof of a durable tradable advantage in either version.
citation: Portfolio allocation and ML — What can I honestly say about the ML conclusion? [common]

text:
The original mean-variance allocation is an unconstrained tangency solution
normalised, negative weights clipped and weights capped at 35%. This is a

original method and observed result first, acknowledge its assumptions, and then
describe the specific later correction and its changed result if asked. A later
implementation does not retroactively prove an earlier claim. Do not tune data,

title: RAG design, current status and safe Gemini setup
heading: What is RAG in simple terms?
text:
Retrieval-augmented generation means finding relevant project passages before
asking a language model to explain an answer. Think of an open-book assistant:
it looks up the appropriate notes, then answers with references. It is not
training a new foundation model on this project, and it does not make the finance
methods or historical returns more accurate by itself.

title: RAG design, current status and safe Gemini setup
heading: What material is approved for the assistant?
text:
The manifest explicitly lists curated explanations, original versus later method
notes, typed numerical facts and their frozen provenance. It includes identity,
navigation, beginner finance and interview limitations. It does not ingest the
whole working folder, private files, HANDOFF.md, API keys, private chats or
arbitrary comments. Trusted application instructions stay outside the searchable
documents. Retrieved material is evidence, not permission to execute instructions.
citation: RAG design, current status and safe Gemini setup — What material is approved for the assistant? [common]

title: RAG design, current status and safe Gemini setup
heading: What is implemented now and what still needs connection?
text:
The package contains readable notes, heading-based passages, version metadata,
fact lookup, local lexical search, basic FAQ responses and reference tests. The
Ask the project page connects this retrieval to optional Gemini generation using
a server-side key and visitor consent. Without the key or consent, it displays
relevant source passages directly; basic identity/help needs no model call.
No semantic embeddings, live market feed, calculator tool or trading connection
is implemented. Code and offline/mock tests do not verify a live deployment or
Gemini answer quality; the actual running application must report its status.
citation: RAG design, current status and safe Gemini setup — What is implemented now and what still needs connection? [common]

title: RAG design, current status and safe Gemini setup
heading: How would a question travel through the finished assistant?
text:
The application supplies the selected research version and enabled capabilities.
Basic identity/help receives an immediate local response. A project question
retrieves up to four approved passages for that version plus relevant structured
saved values when applicable. With consent and a configured key, Gemini receives
that evidence, trusted instructions and a few recent same-version messages.
The app validates the response structure and source IDs before showing an AI
answer; a bad response falls back to notes. Those checks cannot prove that each
claim is supported. An active-scenario calculator remains a separate future
validated Python tool, not arithmetic invented by the language model.

Embeddings represent meaning numerically for retrieval; Google documents a Gemini
embedding interface for tasks such as semantic search. Model names, availability,
quotas, permissions and pricing must be checked when integrating rather than
assumed from this preparation: [Google — Embeddings](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/embeddings).
citation: RAG design, current status and safe Gemini setup — How would a question travel through the finished assistant? [common]

title: RAG design, current status and safe Gemini setup
heading: Will the owner need to provide a Gemini API key? Will visitors need one?
text:
The optional server-side Gemini integration needs an authorised key for the
configured project. The app owner can supply it privately through Streamlit
Secrets; visitors need not each enter their own key in this design. Do not paste
the key into a chat, commit it to Git or expose it to the browser. Preparing this
knowledge base requires no key and makes no paid model requests.

[Google — API key security](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/api-key) explains
keeping keys confidential and server-side. [Streamlit — Community Cloud secrets](https://docs.streamlit.io/deploy/streamlit-community-cloud/deploy-your-app/secrets-management)
explains private deployment configuration. The owner's quota/billing applies to
requests made with their key. The app limits question/history length, caps output,
does not automatically retry, and applies session/cooldown limits plus a
best-effort per-running-server daily allowance. The allowance resets after a
process restart and is not coordinated across replicas: it is NOT a strict
billing cap. Provider-side quotas or stronger shared enforcement are needed
before a high-traffic public launch.
citation: RAG design, current status and safe Gemini setup — Will the owner need to provide a Gemini API key? Will visitors need one? [common]

title: RAG design, current status and safe Gemini setup
heading: What privacy and cost boundaries should a public chatbot have?
text:
When Gemini is enabled, submitted questions and selected passages will be sent to
the configured external provider. Do not claim all processing is local or ask
for confidential company records or personal financial details. Applicable
provider terms and the project's billing configuration must be reviewed before
launch. Keep only the necessary conversation context, limit question length and
request frequency, and handle unavailable service without exposing secrets.
No permanent personal memory is implemented in this package.
citation: RAG design, current status and safe Gemini setup — What privacy and cost boundaries should a public chatbot have? [common]

title: RAG design, current status and safe Gemini setup
heading: How will we know the assistant is useful rather than just fluent?
text:
Use reference questions covering basic finance, identity, calculations, source
citations, missing information, version separation and unsafe requests. Check
retrieval separately from final answers: correct evidence in the top passages
does not prove that a model used it correctly. Compare a simple keyword or
full-context baseline against semantic retrieval for this small corpus. Then
check factual correctness, citation support, abstention, latency and cost with
actual model responses. Current lexical smoke tests are not LLM answer accuracy.
citation: RAG design, current status and safe Gemini setup — How will we know the assistant is useful rather than just fluent? [common]

title: RAG design, current status and safe Gemini setup
heading: What can be claimed on a future AI/ML résumé?
text:
Once integrated and tested, describe the actual retrieval method, Gemini-based
generation, source citations, evaluation and deployment. Finance portfolio ML
and RAG answer generation are different components. Do not say a foundation model
was trained, a semantic system was deployed, hallucinations were eliminated or
an accuracy score was achieved merely because a knowledge base was prepared.
The implementation now includes version-filtered lexical RAG, optional Gemini
generation, a Streamlit chat interface and offline/mock checks. Public deployment
and live-model quality must be verified separately. Do not claim semantic search,
measured model accuracy or a production-grade billing/security boundary.
citation: RAG design, current status and safe Gemini setup — What can be claimed on a future AI/ML résumé? [common]
